source: Top customer questions from Google autocomplete (the AnswerThePublic method: keyword + who/what/how/can/does/should...), ranked by frequency, Nov 2026
items: How much does a locksmith cost in {{city}}?

At {{business}}, house and car lockouts start at $65, lock rekeying at $35 per lock, car key replacement and key fob programming at $85, and smart lock installation at $55. The estimate is free, and the technician gives you a firm price before any work starts, so there are no surprise charges. All starting prices are on our services page.
What should I do if I lost my car key and have no spare?

Don't tow the car to the dealer. Call a mobile automotive locksmith: we come to where the car is, cut a new key from the vehicle's key code or the lock, and program it to the immobilizer on the spot. Have your ID and the registration or title ready. Car key replacement starts at $85 in {{city}}.
Can a locksmith make a car key without the original?

Yes. We cut a new key from the VIN key code or by decoding the door lock, then program the transponder or smart key to your car, for almost every make and model. You don't need the original key, only proof that the car is yours.
Can a locksmith program a key fob?

Yes. We program remote-head keys, smart keys and push-to-start fobs on site with dealer-level tools, usually in minutes and for less than the dealer charges. Key fob programming starts at $85, and we can make a spare at the same visit.
Can a lost car key be deactivated?
Yes, for most cars. When we program your new key, we erase the lost key from the car's immobilizer, so it can no longer start the engine even if someone finds it.
How much does it cost to rekey a lock?
Lock rekeying starts at $35 per lock. We rekey every door in your home or business to one new key in a single visit, without replacing the hardware, and the old keys stop working immediately.
Should I rekey or change my locks?

Rekey when the locks work well and you just need the old keys to stop working, for example after moving in, losing a key or a roommate moving out. It is faster and cheaper. Replace the locks when they are worn, damaged or low-grade, or when you want an upgrade such as a deadbolt, a high-security lock or a smart lock. The technician will tell you honestly which one makes sense.
What should I do if I'm locked out of my house?

First check other doors, and whether a family member, roommate or landlord has a spare key. If not, call a local licensed locksmith and ask for the price up front. We open house and apartment doors without damage in most cases, house lockouts start at $65, and we reach most of {{city}} within the hour.
Will a locksmith damage my lock or door?

Usually not. For the vast majority of house and car lockouts we pick or bypass the lock, or use an air wedge on a car door, so nothing is damaged. Drilling is a last resort for broken or high-security locks, and the technician always tells you before doing it.
Does a locksmith need proof that I own the house or car?

Yes. A reputable locksmith checks that you live at the address or own the vehicle before opening it. Have your photo ID ready; if your documents are inside, showing a bill, lease, registration or title once the door is open is enough.
How long does it take a locksmith to arrive?

Most lockouts in {{city}} are reached within 20 to 40 minutes, and nearly every call within the hour. The dispatcher gives you an arrival time when you call, and most lockouts take only a few minutes once the technician is there.
Are you open on weekends and holidays?
Yes. {{business}} is open 7 AM to 11 PM, 7 days a week, including weekends and holidays. Call {{phone}} or book online.
Do smart locks need Wi-Fi, and can a locksmith install one?

Most smart locks work without Wi-Fi, using Bluetooth and the keypad; Wi-Fi or a bridge is only needed to unlock remotely or get alerts away from home. We install, pair and test August, Yale, Schlage Encode, Kwikset Halo and Level smart locks, starting at $55.
Does insurance cover a locksmith or lost car keys?

Sometimes. Many auto policies with comprehensive coverage, roadside assistance plans and some homeowner or renter policies reimburse lockouts or key replacement. Check your policy; we give you an itemized receipt for the claim.
Is {{business}} licensed and insured?

Yes. {{business}} is registered with the Washington State Department of Labor & Industries as a Locks, Security Alarms and Warning Systems specialty contractor (SPEEDLL761BT), and we are insured and background-checked. You can confirm the registration with L&I's Verify a Contractor tool before you book.
